about.title: North Hollywood Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a fatal crash, fall, or other preventable incident happens in North Hollywood, the people left behind often face grief alongside unpaid bills and unanswered questions. California law gives certain family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim against the party responsible. If no immediate family exists, other dependents or heirs may have standing. This is a civil matter, separate from any criminal charges that might follow the same incident, and it moves on its own timeline. Families in North Hollywood, part of Los Angeles County, have two years from the date of death to file, though claims against a government agency carry a much shorter window. Our team can review what happened and explain what a claim might recover, without adding to what you're already carrying.

whyChoose.title: Why North Hollywood Families Choose Us

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, typically the spouse, domestic partner, or children first. We can confirm where your family fits before any paperwork moves forward.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Death, Not Discovery
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, but that window shrinks considerably if a government entity was involved. Acting sooner protects your family's ability to pursue a claim at all.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral costs and lost financial support, but also for harder-to-quantify losses like companionship and guidance. We can help value what's actually owed.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in North Hollywood?
items.answer: Under California law, a spouse, domestic partner, or children typically have first standing to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may be eligible instead. We can review your family's specific situation and confirm who qualifies.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to a criminal case against the person responsible?
items.answer: No, they're separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action seeking compensation for the family. One can proceed even if the other doesn't result in a conviction.

items.question: How much time do we have to file after a death in North Hollywood?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If a government agency, such as a city vehicle or public property, was involved, that deadline is much shorter, so speaking with us early matters.

items.question: Do you charge anything to help us with a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: No. Our team typically works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your family recovers compensation.
